description.narrative: The project will support the Government of the Republic of Uzbekistan's health service optimization process, which aims to improve and expand primary health care services delivered in the rural areas. The proposed project will strengthen the rural health sector by providing the 793 newly established rural family polyclinics with modern diagnostic equipment and health workforce development to expand their service delivery. This will be supported by tools to monitor the government's broader primary health care reform and the project, and include a pilot of a health management information system in a rural region.

description.narrative: Availability of primary healthcare services in rural areas expanded

At least 50% of women and men reported increased confidence in consulting rural polyclinics Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: Completed by 30 June 2024. Baseline and completion surveys completed. Completion survey shows 90.9% of women and men have reported increased confidence in FPs. Q2 2024 - Baseline survey showed that 90% of users of RFPs trust the services, and among users of FDPs their share was 86.2%. Data Source: Health-seeking behavior survey before and after the project

Readiness to provide antenatal and reproductive health services for women through ultrasound for women met by 70% of rural family polyclinics Achievement: 90 Progress/Status: Completed (99.7%) Q2 2024 - All 801 RFPs have received ultrasound machines and installation of the equipment was completed. - 8 training centers, and SamMI and AndMI received 1 USG each, and the Center for the Development of Professional Qualifications of Medical Workers received 3 USGs. - Due to the fact that not all regional training centers are involved in training process under the project, according the MOH's instruction letters, 5 USG machines have been distributed to 5 PHC facilities, which are not the originally planned sites. - 799 (99.7%) RFPs which received USG machines have USG operators (updated figures to be provided by PIU/EA) - Around 580 RFP ultrasound operators completed training and received certificates before 2019 (not under project) and 1,418 RFP doctors completed training program and received certificates since 2019 (figures to be verified). - All equipment installation and training was completed.
- On 24 April 2020, contract No. PHCIP / ICB-G1-01 UMI-2020/08 for Lot 1 “Delivery of Ultrasound” in the amount of $8.15 million was signed. On 27 November 2020 820 ultrasound machines arrived at the customs warehouse in Tashkent. Сustoms clearance for the equipment was carried out. Data Source: World Health Organization facility service and readiness assessment

Readiness to provide electrocardiograph met by 70% of rural family polyclinics Achievement: 70 Progress/Status: Completed (100%) Q2 2024 - All 801 RFPs have received ECG devices. In addition, 8 training centers, and SamMI and AndMI received 1 ECG each, and the Center for the Development of Professional Qualifications of Medical Workers received 3 ECGs. Due to the fact that not all regional training centers are involved in training process under the project, according the MOH's instruction letters 5 ECG machines have been distributed to 5 PHC facilities, which are not the originally planned sites. - 801 RFPs (100%) have trained ECG operators. Most of the training session took place at the regional branches of the republican center for advanced training of middle medical personnel. Nearly 14,369 nurses and approximately 1,828 doctors had been trained for ECG operators between 2019 and 2023, however these figures need to be verified. - MOH conducted an inventory of the status of the power supply to PHC facilities and propose remedial solutions in case of deficiencies in this regard. The update was in line with WHO definition of power supply that a facility routinely has electricity for lights and communication (at a minimum) from any power source during normal working hours.
- On 14 September 2020, 820 ECG devices in the amount 0.7 million US dollars under contract no. PHP/IMG 1-02 UMI-2020/07 arrived at the customs warehouse in Tashkent and transferred to LLC “Uzmedimpex” warehouse. Data Source: World Health Organization facility service and readiness assessment
